term: "False Negative"

## Simple explanation

A false negative occurs when a model fails to detect a condition that is
actually present. For example, a screening model may classify a
condition-positive case as negative.

## Technical explanation

In binary classification, a false negative (FN) is an instance with a
positive actual label and a negative predicted label. The false-negative
rate is $FN/(FN+TP)$, while recall is $TP/(TP+FN)$. These metrics
depend on the class definition, labels, and decision threshold.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

False negatives can allow fraud, defects, or safety issues to go
undetected. Their consequences may differ substantially from false
positives, so threshold selection should reflect the use case and its
error costs.

## How it works

The model produces a score and a decision rule assigns a positive label
only when that score meets a threshold. A positive example below the
threshold becomes a false negative. Lowering the threshold may reduce
false negatives while increasing false positives.

## Practical example

For a penguin-versus-ostrich classifier where ostrich is the positive
class, an ostrich image predicted as penguin is a false negative.

## Common misconceptions

- A false negative is not the same as a false-positive error.
- Reducing false negatives may increase false positives.
- The term depends on which class is designated positive.
